location: Strip Processing switch, effect chips (1080p, 4:2:0, 29.97), ⇧⌘B in Feed menu and dropdown, ⋯ popover Processing section
issue: Effect and bypass changes that alter the output format interrupt the Zoom feed, but every surface presents them as harmless one-click toggles with no warning, confirmation or deferral.
evidence: CaptureController.reconfigure() resets the sample factory and sets message 'Updating output…'; CameraSink.send() throws 'Frame does not match the virtual camera's negotiated format and timing' on a size/pixel-format/duration change; CaptureController then disconnects the camera, schedules a reconnect after cameraRetryInterval and counts an outage. The extension emits black after 0.5 s without a producer frame (README). README: 'consumers must accept the selected format'. Downscale, Color, Frame rate and Processing (bypass = 2160p x422) all change the format; LUT alone does not.
scenario: Mid-call the user presses ⇧⌘B or clicks the 1080p chip to compare. Zoom's picture goes black or freezes during the reconnect, or never recovers if Zoom rejects 2160p 10-bit 4:2:2.
recommendation: Classify every control as live-safe or disruptive. When the feed's camera is in use (or it's on air in Program), disruptive changes show an inline confirmation ('Changes the format Zoom receives; the picture blanks for about a second') or are staged as 'Apply at next stop'. LUT stays instant. Chips become read-only summaries while the camera is in use; editing moves to the ⋯ popover with the warning.
alternatives: 'Pending changes · Apply' bar that applies all format changes in one renegotiation
Meeting lock: format-changing controls disabled while a consumer is connected, with an explicit Unlock
Hold-to-toggle for chips while live
affects: states (new 'Updating output…' and 'Change will interrupt Zoom' states)

location: Feed picture click; dropdown cut thumbnails
issue: A single click on a feed picture is defined as 'cut Program to this feed', while monitor-tools defines the same click as 'focus this tile' (and focus also drives ⌃⌥F/⌃⌥C and likely the selected feed). One gesture has three meanings, one of them visible in the meeting.
evidence: main-expanded legend 2: 'Click a picture or press ⌃1/⌃2 to cut.' program-view: 'Click a source to cut.' monitor-tools: 'Click a tile to focus it (blue ring). Shortcuts act on the focused tile only, as today.' Current code: MonitorWorkspaceShell surface() uses TapGesture to set focusedTile. menubar (a): 'Click a camera to cut'.
scenario: During a Program meeting the user clicks Feed 2's picture to turn on zebra or freeze it; Zoom immediately cuts to Feed 2. In the dropdown, a click meant to open the menu row lands on a thumbnail and cuts.
recommendation: Picture click only focuses/selects. Cuts happen from explicit cut controls (toolbar cut buttons, strip 'Cut to Feed N', ⌃n) or a deliberate gesture. In the dropdown, thumbnails show tally only; cuts are menu items ('Cut to Feed 2 ⌃2').
alternatives: Double-click a picture to cut
⌥-click to cut, with a hover hint
Click arms the cut (green 'Take' button appears), second click or Return takes it (preview/program 'Take' model)

location: Stop Feed / Stop Feeds ⌘↩ (dropdown, Feed menu), ⋯ popover
issue: Stopping a feed also ends its recording and its Zoom output, but every Stop Feed control is a plain one-key/one-click action with no mention of either consequence.
evidence: AppModel.stop(): manuallyStoppedFeeds.insert, feedCoordinator.stop(selectedFeedID), recordingModel.stop(feedID: selectedFeedID). Recording also stops on any stopped capture update (AppModel onUpdate: update.stopped → recordingModel.stop). Pages: menubar 'Stop Feed ⌘↩' and 'Stop Feeds ⌘↩' rows next to Processing; app-menus Feed 'Stop Feed ⌘↩'. No page states that it ends the take.
scenario: The user means to stop recording, picks 'Stop Feed' (top row of the dropdown, highlighted position) or presses ⌘↩ with Ultracam frontmost. Zoom goes black and the backup take finalizes.
recommendation: When the feed is recording or its camera is in use, Stop Feed asks first: 'Stop Feed 1? Zoom loses the camera and the recording (12:31) is finished.' [Stop Feed] [Cancel]. Move Stop Feed below the recording rows in the dropdown; keep ⌘↩ but route it through the same confirmation when anything is live.
alternatives: Disable Stop Feed while recording ('Stop the recording first')
Undo-style 5 s grace: 'Stopping Feed 1… Undo' before teardown
Hold ⌘↩ for 1 s while live

location: Expanded strip Pause | Stop buttons; record button turning into stop; collapsed strip record button next to ⋯
issue: Ending a take is a single unguarded click on a control that sits beside Pause (same size and style) or beside ⋯ (9 pt gap) and shares its target with Record. A finished take can't be resumed; it becomes a new file.
evidence: r3.js strip(): Pause and Stop as adjacent identical .btn (24 pt), plus the 30 pt recbtn that is 'on' (= stop) while recording. Collapsed strip: recbtn sm (30 pt) then btn icon ⋯ (24 pt) with 9 pt gap. main-collapsed hover row adds Pause/Stop inline. RecordingModel.stop finalizes the movie.
scenario: Reaching for ⋯ on a collapsed strip during a meeting, or for Pause, the user clicks Stop; the backup take ends and the next segment is a separate file (or nothing, if they don't notice).
recommendation: One primary record control per strip: red Record → while recording becomes a square Stop that needs confirmation or a 1 s press-and-hold (with a progress ring), Pause stays a separate, visually secondary control placed away from Stop. Collapsed strips show state only; stop lives in hover controls with spacing ≥ 16 pt from ⋯.
alternatives: Stop asks only if the take is longer than 1 min
'Take ended · Resume as new take' toast with one click

issue: The most prominent control in the window is a Stop All button whose label is elapsed time, not an action. One click finalizes every recording, and its look is identical to the Record All button it replaces.
evidence: r3.js toolbar(): tb-prominent red with stop icon and recLabel ('12:31 · 2'); main-expanded legend 5 calls it 'Record All shows elapsed time and the number of takes'. standalone uses 'Stop All · 12:31'. ⌥⌘R toggles Record All / Stop All (app-menus).
scenario: The user glances at the timer and clicks it expecting details; both backup takes stop. Pressing ⌥⌘R twice (once to check) starts new takes.
recommendation: Split status from action: the toolbar shows a REC status chip (elapsed, count) that opens the recording popover; Stop All lives in that popover and the Record menu with a confirmation listing the takes. Use separate shortcuts for Record All and Stop All, or make ⌥⌘R start-only.
alternatives: Keep the button but label it 'Stop All' with elapsed as secondary text, plus confirmation when > 1 take
Hold-to-stop on the toolbar button

issue: Keyboard and menu commands act on an invisible 'selected feed'. With strips making all feeds equal, the user can't see which camera ⇧⌘B or Stop Feed ⌘↩ will hit.
evidence: AppModel: pipelineEnabled, start(), stop(), chooseLUT() all target selectedFeedID. app-menus: Feed menu header 'acts on Feed 1'; menubar labels the Processing row 'Feed 1' only in Program state. main-expanded shows no selection marker (sidebar row 1 has a subtle fill, ambiguous with tally).
scenario: Two-camera meeting: the user clicked Feed 2's strip earlier, then presses ⇧⌘B intending Feed 1. Feed 2 (on air) bypasses, changing format mid-call (see L2-01).
recommendation: Either show selection unmistakably (selected strip/picture gets an accent outline distinct from tally; menu items name the feed: 'Bypass Feed 2 ⇧⌘B') or remove the global commands and make every command feed-scoped (Feed ▸ Feed 1 ▸ …, strip ⋯). Never let a disruptive shortcut target a feed whose name isn't in the command.
alternatives: Selection follows the focused tile only, with the name echoed in the toolbar title
Disruptive global shortcuts disabled when > 1 feed is live

location: Program-mode 'Stop Feeds ⌘↩' (dropdown a), toolbar/Feed menu Stop
issue: In Program mode Start starts every source, but Stop only stops the selected feed (and its recording). The dropdown's 'Stop Feeds' label promises the opposite.
evidence: AppModel.startFeed(): in .program starts every enabled descriptor with a device. AppModel.stop(): feedCoordinator.stop(selectedFeedID) and recordingModel.stop(feedID: selectedFeedID) only; other headless sources keep running and recording. menubar (a): 'Stop Feeds ⌘↩'.
scenario: After the meeting the user chooses 'Stop Feeds' believing everything stopped; Feed 2 keeps capturing and recording to disk.
recommendation: Make the label match the behavior per mode ('Stop Feed 1' vs 'Stop All Feeds'), and design an explicit 'Stop All Feeds' (ending all takes, with confirmation). Flag the start/stop asymmetry for the runtime (L8).
alternatives: End Session command: stops all feeds and takes and lists what was saved

location: Manual cut while Auto is on
issue: Manual cuts while Auto switching is on are sent to the director as a manual override, but no page shows what happens next (does Auto hold, cut back, or turn off?). The operator can't predict whether their cut will stick.
evidence: AppModel.requestProgramCut → autoSwitcherBridge.manualOverride(cameraID:at:); NaturalTalkingHeadSettings has manualHold. states shows 'Auto holding' (shot timer) and 'Auto off · manual', but no 'Manual override · Auto resumes in …' state; toolbar cut buttons sit next to the Auto toggle with no hint.
scenario: The user cuts to Feed 2 for a demo; 3 s later Auto cuts back to Feed 1 mid-sentence.
recommendation: Design a 'Manual hold' state: after a manual cut with Auto on, show 'Held on Feed 2 · Auto resumes after the shot timer / Resume Auto now', and decide (with the director's real behavior) whether Auto pauses until resumed. Show it on the tally badge, sidebar Program section and dropdown.
alternatives: Manual cut turns Auto off (explicit, simplest)
Setting: 'Manual cuts pause Auto' (maps to manualHold)

location: ⌃1–⌃4 cut vs ⌘1–⌘4 select feed vs ⌥⌘1–⌥⌘4 layout; ⌘R record/stop selected
issue: Three families of number shortcuts differ only by modifier, and the one that changes the meeting (⌃n cut) is the easiest to hit by mistake. ⌘R (proposed record/stop) is 'reload' muscle memory elsewhere, and it can stop a take.
evidence: app-menus shortcut table: ⌃1–⌃4 Cut (proposed), ⌘1–⌘4 Select feed, ⌥⌘1–⌥⌘4 Layout, ⌘R Record/Stop selected feed. spec §6 lists the same.
scenario: The user means ⌘2 (select Feed 2 to adjust it) and presses ⌃2: Zoom cuts. Or presses ⌘R expecting a refresh and stops the recording.
recommendation: Make ⌘R start-only (never stop), and stop via a confirmed command. Keep cut shortcuts but give them visible feedback (tally flash + 'Cut to Feed 2 · ⌘Z-like Undo cut' for 3 s, which cuts back). Consider dropping ⌘1–⌘4 select if selection is removed (L2-06).
alternatives: Cuts on plain 1–4 only in Program view
Require Return to take an armed cut

issue: The quit sheet covers recordings only. Quitting while a meeting app is using Ultracam's camera cuts the meeting's video with no warning.
evidence: states 'Quit while recording': 'Quit stops capture and waits for active takes to finish.' AppDelegate.applicationShouldTerminate only defers for active recordings. Settings General: 'Quit waits for active recordings to finish.' No state for 'camera in use by Zoom'.
scenario: The user quits Ultracam from the dropdown during a call to tidy the menu bar; Zoom's video goes black.
recommendation: When any virtual camera is in use, ⌘Q shows 'Zoom is using Ultracam · Quitting stops the camera in the meeting' [Quit] [Cancel], combined with the recording summary if takes are active. Offer 'Close Window' as the default for users who just want it out of the way.
alternatives: Quit becomes 'Hide' while a consumer is connected unless ⌥ is held

issue: The brief output interruption after a configuration change (and the camera reconnect after a transport error) has no design. The current app's 'Applying change…' and 'Updating output…' messages and the camera-outage state are missing from every page, so after a disruptive change the user can't tell whether Zoom is getting a picture.
evidence: CaptureController.reconfigure sets message 'Updating output…'; on send failure cameraMessage 'Camera output disconnected — …' and a timed reconnect. Inventory §2.1 'Applying change…'. grep finds no 'Updating output', 'Applying change' or reconnect state in r3 pages.
scenario: After toggling Downscale, Zoom shows black for a second; the Ultracam picture still looks live, so the user assumes it's Zoom's fault, or toggles again (another renegotiation).
recommendation: Add an output-health state to the tally/output row: 'Updating output…' (spinner) → 'Reconnecting to Zoom…' (orange) → normal. Show it on the picture badge, the strip output row, the status bar output segment and the dropdown.
alternatives: Toast 'Zoom output paused for 0.8 s' after each renegotiation

location: Failure mid-take: HDMI lost, destination drive disconnected
issue: Mid-take failures that matter most for a backup recorder are not designed: HDMI signal loss while recording (detection stays armed, so the take continues with no frames, or ends), and the recording drive being unplugged. Only 'disk low' and 'dropped frames' exist.
evidence: CaptureController watchdog: with startAutomatic, signal loss → 'No video signal — waiting for HDMI.' (capture not stopped). RecordingModel: 'Recording stopped after a source error.' states covers No signal (not recording), Failed, disk low; four-up Feed 3 'No signal' is idle. No 'signal lost while recording' or 'drive disconnected' card.
scenario: The camera's HDMI cable is bumped 20 minutes into a meeting; the user doesn't know whether the backup has a gap, stopped, or resumed.
recommendation: Design 'Signal lost · recording continues (gap 00:03)' vs 'Recording stopped: signal lost · Start new take' depending on actual recorder behavior (verify), and 'Drive disconnected · take saved up to 12:31 (recoverable)'. Make both visible on the strip, picture, status bar and menu bar icon (attention dot).
alternatives: Auto-start a new take when the signal returns (proposal, NEW)

issue: Recover is offered during an active recording. Recovery copies complete fragments of a large interrupted movie, likely to the same drive the live takes are writing to, which risks I/O contention and dropped frames in the live take.
evidence: README: 'Recovery copies complete fragments into a separate _Recovered.mov without re-encoding'. r3 sidebar shows 'Interrupted · Recover' while 'Backup · 2 feeds 12:31' is recording on the same 8TB drive.
scenario: During a meeting the user clicks Recover on yesterday's take; a multi-GB copy runs on the 8TB drive and today's takes start dropping frames.
recommendation: While any take is recording, Recover is disabled with 'Available when recordings stop', or it asks first ('Recovery copies 41 GB on 8TB while recording; this may cause dropped frames').
alternatives: Queue the recovery to run automatically after recording stops

location: NEW 'Record with camera apps' + 'Stop when the last camera app closes'
issue: The proposed auto-stop can end a recording the user started deliberately (standalone) when an unrelated camera client closes, for example Zoom's settings preview.
evidence: settings Recording/Automation: 'Stop when the last camera app closes' (NEW) with no scope. README: 'Zoom's camera settings preview also counts as camera use.' Current code keeps feeds running while recording (reconcileAutomaticFeed guard !recording), so this would be new behavior.
scenario: The user records a standalone interview, opens Zoom to check something, and closes it; auto-stop finalizes the interview take.
recommendation: Scope auto-stop to takes that auto-record started ('Stop backup takes it started'); manually started takes are never auto-stopped. Show the origin on the strip ('Backup · started with Zoom').
alternatives: Grace period: auto-stop after 30 s without a client, with 'Keep Recording' in a notification

location: Toolbar cut buttons next to Auto toggle; layout picker and collapse toggle in the same toolbar row
issue: Meeting-affecting controls (cuts) sit in the same glass row as view-only controls (layout, collapse strips), styled alike, with no separation. Mis-clicks between a view change and a cut are likely, and view controls don't read as safe.
evidence: r3.js toolbar(): cuts group (Feed 1 red / Feed 2 green outline / Auto) directly followed by the layout group and the collapse toggle; same tb-group glass style and height.
scenario: Reaching for Side by Side, the user clicks the 'Feed 2' cut pill.
recommendation: Group live controls (cut, Auto, Record) on the trailing side behind a ToolbarSpacer, and view controls (layout, collapse, sidebar) leading or in the View menu. Make view controls visually quieter.
alternatives: Move cut buttons into a dedicated cut bar only in Program view and the strips

location: Sleep / lid close / display sleep while live
issue: Nothing tells the user that closing the lid or system sleep will stop the meeting feed and recordings. The app prevents idle sleep while capturing, but that's invisible.
evidence: CaptureController begins ProcessInfo activity [.userInitiated, .latencyCritical] ('Live UltraStudio video processing'), which prevents idle sleep only. No page covers sleep or lid close.
scenario: The user closes a laptop lid for a moment during a recording break; capture and the take stop.
recommendation: Status bar/Info note 'Preventing idle sleep while live'. After wake, a strip state explains what was interrupted ('Stopped by sleep at 14:22 · take saved').

issue: There's no single way to protect a live session. Every disruptive control (bypass, effects, stop feed, stop take, cut by click, input/LUT changes) is always armed, and the fixes above have to be applied piecemeal.
evidence: Aggregate of L2-01..L2-06; no lock or meeting mode on any page.
scenario: A presenter wants to hand off the laptop or present from it without risking the stream.
recommendation: Propose (NEW) 'Live Lock' (toolbar padlock, ⌃⌘L): while on, disruptive controls need confirmation or are disabled; cut, record and Auto stay available. It turns on automatically when a camera client connects (setting). Pair with the per-control rules above rather than replacing them.
alternatives: No global mode; rely on per-control guards (L2-01, -03, -04, -05)

evidence: main-expanded: 'Click a picture … to cut'; program-view and menubar same; monitor-tools: 'Click a tile to focus it'; MonitorWorkspaceShell TapGesture focuses. See L2-02.
AppModel commands target selectedFeedID; no visible selection in main-expanded; Feed menu says 'acts on Feed 1'. See L2-06.

CameraSink.send throws on a format mismatch → CaptureController disconnect + timed reconnect (outage); reconfigure() resets output ('Updating output…'). Applies to Downscale, Color, Frame rate and Processing/bypass, not LUT alone. See L2-01, L2-11.
Toolbar stop-all labelled only by elapsed time; strip Stop vs Stop Feed vs record-button-as-stop; Program-mode 'Stop Feeds' stops only the selected feed. See L2-05, L2-07.
AppModel.startFeed starts all enabled sources in .program; stop() stops only selectedFeedID and its recording. See L2-07.
Strip Stop, toolbar Stop All, dropdown Stop Feed/Stop All and ⌘↩ are single unguarded actions; Stop Feed also ends the take (AppModel.stop → recordingModel.stop). See L2-03, L2-04, L2-05.
From a live-safety view the repeated REC indicators are reassuring, but the toolbar instance doubles as a Stop All action (L2-05). Echoes should be status-only; one place should own the action.
